learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the secrets of finding the Highest Common Factor and Lowest Common Multiple to easily solve puzzles about sharing and repeating events!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Every big number is built out of smaller prime numbers multiplied together. Prime factorisation is like taking a toy apart to see the exact building blocks used to make it!
The Highest Common Factor (HCF) is the biggest number that can divide two or more numbers perfectly. We use it when we want to cut things into the largest possible equal pieces without any leftovers.

The Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) is the smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. We use LCM to figure out when two repeating events, like flashing traffic lights or ringing bells, will happen at the exact same time!

fun_activity.title: 🧩 The Digroz Notification Planner
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you send two types of study alerts on your learning app. Alert A goes out every 12 minutes, and Alert B goes out every 18 minutes. Find their LCM to calculate the exact minute both alerts will beep on a student's phone together!

quick_recap: ⭐ Prime factorisation breaks composite numbers down into purely prime multipliers.
⭐ Use HCF when dividing items into the largest equal groups possible.
⭐ Use LCM to find the smallest common interval when cycles will overlap.
